custom.name: auto-session4-no-silent-build
custom.message: Learned from session 4: Silent build failures hide missing tools. Let builds fail loudly or check at runtime with which.

custom.name: auto-session4-pydantic-schema-sync
custom.message: Learned from session 4: Verify Pydantic response schemas include all ORM model fields. Missing extracted_path hid the action buttons.

custom.name: auto-session5-no-scalar-one-or-none-on-fk
custom.message: Learned from session 5: scalar_one_or_none() crashes with MultipleResultsFound on one-to-many relations. Use .order_by().limit(1) or .all() instead.

custom.name: auto-session5-yara-no-unreferenced-strings
custom.message: Learned from session 5: Every YARA string must appear in the condition. Unreferenced strings cause compilation errors.

custom.name: auto-review-no-raw-join-in-sandbox
custom.message: Learned from review S13: Use validate_path() instead of os.path.join for paths under firmware root. Raw join follows symlinks without sandbox checks.

custom.name: auto-review-no-shell-interpolation
custom.message: Learned from review S2/S4: Use shlex.quote() for all variables interpolated into shell commands. Prefer create_subprocess_exec (list form) over sh -c.

custom.name: auto-review-no-commit-in-tool-handler
custom.message: Learned from review K1: Use context.db.flush() in tool handlers. The outer MCP dispatch handles commit — committing here prevents rollback on partial failures.

custom.name: auto-standalone-dockerignore-venv
custom.message: Learned from standalone binary campaign: Ensure .dockerignore excludes .venv -- COPY . . will overwrite the Docker-built venv with the host venv, causing Python version mismatches and missing modules.

custom.name: auto-standalone-lief-enum-case
custom.message: Learned from standalone binary campaign: LIEF Mach-O CPU_TYPE enums are UPPERCASE (X86_64, ARM64), not lowercase. Always verify with dir().

custom.name: auto-session19-venv-which
custom.message: Learned from session 19: In Docker with uv/venv, CLI tools from pip packages land in /app/.venv/bin/ not system PATH. Use: shutil.which(tool) or shutil.which(tool, path="/app/.venv/bin")

custom.name: auto-docker-opt-verify-ldd
custom.message: Learned from docker-image-optimization: Verify runtime deps with ldd before trusting comments about which packages are needed. Comments rot faster than code.

custom.name: auto-fwid-api-function-missing-firmwareId
custom.message: Learned from S37 firmware-id bug: Every file API function must accept firmwareId param since the backend resolve_firmware dependency uses it for scoping.

custom.name: auto-s37-case-insensitive-fnmatch
custom.message: Learned from S37: User-facing file search should be case-insensitive. Use fnmatch.fnmatch(name.lower(), pattern.lower()) instead.

custom.name: auto-extraction-roots-no-direct-extracted-path
custom.message: Learned from feature-extraction-integrity (CLAUDE.md rule 16): Filesystem walks MUST use get_detection_roots(firmware) from app/services/firmware_paths.py - firmware.extracted_path is ONE rootfs and misses scatter-zip siblings, multi-archive containers, and nested unblob output. Per-binary flows (emulation/fuzzing/device/sandbox) may still use extracted_path. Originally uncovered by DPCS10 md1dsp.img bug + RespArray ZIP regression.

custom.name: auto-classifier-magic-offset-beyond-buffer
custom.message: Learned from feature-classifier-patterns-mcu-kernel: The detector reads only detector._MAGIC_READ_BYTES (64) bytes into `magic`. Indexing past 0x40 (64) silently fails to match. If a new format needs a deeper header check (e.g. iMX-RT BOOT_DATA @ 0x1000), widen _MAGIC_READ_BYTES with a rationale OR route through a per-format parser in parsers/, do not add an unreachable index.

custom.name: auto-intake-sweep-1-no-stat-docker-sock
custom.message: Learned from intake-sweep Phase 1 (commit bac49ea, /health/deep regression 29dba35): stat-based /var/run/docker.sock presence checks fail after the docker-socket-proxy migration because the raw socket is no longer mounted. Probe via get_docker_client().containers.list(limit=1) instead -- verifies BOTH DOCKER_HOST connectivity AND the proxy CONTAINERS allowlist.

custom.name: auto-intake-sweep-1-no-docker-from-env
custom.message: Learned from intake-sweep Phase 1 Stream D (commit bac49ea -- 10 sites across 8 files migrated): use get_docker_client() from app.utils.docker_client instead of docker.from_env(). The factory honours settings.docker_host which routes through the socket proxy; direct from_env() bypasses the proxy and breaks emulation/fuzzing/terminal flows once the raw socket mount is removed.

custom.name: auto-wave3-pydantic-extra-ignore-on-api-schemas
custom.message: Learned from intake-sweep Wave 3 stream beta (DeviceInfo BROM bug): Pydantic extra='ignore' on API-boundary schemas silently strips fields sent by the service layer -- DeviceInfo dropped 4 BROM fields, surfacing as (dev as any).mode === undefined at runtime with zero compile-time signal. Prefer extra='forbid' (loud drift) or explicit field declarations. Use extra='allow' only for ingestion DTOs with a documented reason.

custom.name: auto-wave3-frontend-tsc-no-noemit
custom.message: Learned from intake-sweep Waves 1+2+3 (CLAUDE.md Rule #24): wairz frontend tsconfig uses files: [] + project references; tsc --noEmit exits 0 silently without descending into referenced projects (Rule #17 silent-CLI-exit instance). Use npx tsc -b --force. Rule-17 canary mandatory once per session before trusting any green typecheck output: write a known-bad .ts file, run the command, confirm it fails.

custom.name: auto-wave3-intake-yaml-status-lowercase
custom.message: Learned from intake-sweep Wave 3 stream gamma: intake YAML status: values should be lowercase (completed, pending, partial, draft, active) for close-out query coherence. Capitalised values work but break case-sensitive greps (grep -l 'status: completed' misses capital-C entries; close-out queries must use grep -li). Status-bump should land in the same commit that ships the intake's work, not wait for a maintenance-sweep.

custom.name: auto-fleet-worktree-requires-worktree-add
custom.message: Learned from intake-sweep sessions 435cb5c2+198243b8 (CLAUDE.md Rule #23 refined by Wave-3 evidence): git checkout -b feat/{branch} ALONE is insufficient under shared on-disk checkout -- alpha and gamma saw 4 cross-stream commit-sweep incidents across 14 commits when they only used branch-checkout. Beta had 0 sweeps in 4 commits AFTER running git worktree add .worktrees/stream-{name} -b feat/stream-{name}-{date} and operating inside that path. Each parallel sub-agent prompt MUST issue git worktree add (not just git checkout -b) and operate inside .worktrees/<stream>/. The Fleet harness isolation: worktree sentinel is a no-op at the working-tree level.

custom.name: auto-phase5-no-private-scan-cross-module
custom.message: Learned from intake-sweep session 93a4948d Phase 5 (backend-private-api-and-circular-imports P1): do not import the private _scan_credentials / _scan_crypto_material / _scan_shadow helpers from security_audit_service across module boundaries. Use the public dispatcher: `from app.services.security_audit_service import run_scan_subset; run_scan_subset(root, ['credentials','crypto_material','shadow'], findings)`. The private helpers are intentionally internal; the public API hides signature changes and the SCANNERS registry keeps the set of available checks single-sourced.

custom.name: auto-phase5-cache-use-services-cache-helpers
custom.message: Learned from intake-sweep session 93a4948d Phase 5 (backend-cache-module-extraction-and-ttl): use app.services._cache helpers (store_cached / get_cached / exists_cached / invalidate_firmware / cleanup_older_than) instead of hand-rolling the delete-then-insert pattern against AnalysisCache. The helpers are the canonical path — they handle firmware-wide (binary_sha256 IS NULL) keys, issue flush() so callers own commit(), and their delete-then-insert is idempotent without relying on the unique constraint. Exemptions: app/services/_cache.py itself, app/services/export_service.py and app/services/import_service.py (legitimate bulk patterns), test files.

custom.name: auto-frontend-rebuild-not-restart
custom.message: Learned from intake-sweep session 93a4948d (CLAUDE.md Rule #26): `docker compose restart frontend` reuses the stale image — the baked-in `/usr/share/nginx/html/dist` does NOT pick up code changes under `frontend/src/**`. Use `docker compose up -d --build frontend` instead. Session 93a4948d incident: a TypeError thrown in Sidebar.tsx from `projects.map(...)` traced to a frontend container built before Zeta's `unwrap()` helper landed; `projectStore.fetchProjects` was getting `{items:[...]}` from the new backend Page-envelope response, but the pre-Zeta bundle returned that raw to the store. Companion to Rule #8 (backend+worker rebuild discipline).

custom.name: auto-frontend-fake-scan-failed-error
custom.pattern: errors:\s*\[\s*['\"](Scan failed|Security audit failed|YARA scan failed)['\"]\s*\]
custom.message: Learned from session 93a4948d (CLAUDE.md Rule #2x bug-fix cluster): hardcoded fake-error arrays like `errors: ['Scan failed']` inside a `catch {}` block discard the real exception. Replace with `errors: [extractErrorMessage(e, 'Operation failed')]` and bind the exception with `catch (e) { ... }`. The backend is often succeeding while the UI claims failure — root cause is almost always a swallowed axios timeout from the default 30s on a long-running scan/audit endpoint. See .planning/knowledge/wairz-intake-sweep-bug-fixes-2026-04-19-antipatterns.md anti-pattern #1.

custom.name: auto-frontend-long-op-no-explicit-timeout
custom.message: Learned from session 7e8dd7c3 (bug.har complaint + generateSbom timeout + full sweep commit 6814461..ce4bf45): long-running backend calls must declare an explicit timeout: option on the options object — default axios timeout is 30s (client.ts) and these endpoints routinely exceed it, surfacing a fake 'scan failed' to the UI while the backend completes successfully. Common tiers: SECURITY_SCAN_TIMEOUT=600_000 (scans, SBOM, audit, fuzzing analyze/triage, MCP tools, uploads), GHIDRA_ANALYSIS_TIMEOUT=180_000 (decompile, cleaned-code), RADARE2_ANALYSIS_TIMEOUT=90_000 (functions, imports, disasm, binary-info), DEVICE_BRIDGE_TIMEOUT=300_000 (device import/dump). Use the matching constant already defined in the sibling file (findings.ts / sbom.ts pattern). Prior rule defects: (a) verb allowlist missed generate/triage/analyze/capture/decompile/bytecode/sast/cleaned-code/disasm/network-analysis/tools-run; (b) no negative-lookahead check — fired on already-annotated calls. Both fixed.

custom.name: auto-phase5-no-security-audit-service-import
custom.message: Learned from campaign wairz-intake-sweep-2026-04-19 session b56eb487: security_audit_service.py was deleted in Phase 5 part 2 split (commit fb28072); module no longer exists. Use from app.services.security_audit import ... instead.

custom.name: auto-phase5-no-manifest-checks-mixin
custom.message: Learned from campaign wairz-intake-sweep-2026-04-19 session b56eb487: ManifestChecksMixin was removed in Phase 5 part 1 split (commit 1577eaa); inheritance replaced with composition via ManifestChecker. Use from app.services.manifest_checks import ManifestChecker instead.

custom.name: auto-phase5-no-sbom-service-import
custom.message: Learned from campaign wairz-intake-sweep-2026-04-19 session 7e8dd7c3: sbom_service.py was deleted in Phase 5 part 3 split (commit b29ef8f); module no longer exists. Use from app.services.sbom import ... instead (SbomService, IdentifiedComponent, CPE_VENDOR_MAP, etc. are all re-exported from the package __init__.py). Strategy classes live under app.services.sbom.strategies.*

custom.name: auto-phase5-no-emulation-service-import
custom.message: Learned from campaign wairz-intake-sweep-2026-04-19 session 7e8dd7c3: emulation_service.py was deleted in Phase 5 part 5 split (commit c267931); module no longer exists. Use from app.services.emulation import EmulationService instead. Sub-modules (docker_ops, kernel_selection, sysroot_mount, user_mode, system_mode) can be imported directly if needed — e.g. from app.services.emulation.docker_ops import copy_dir_to_container for free-function access.

custom.name: auto-phase5-no-mobsfscan-service-import
custom.message: Learned from campaign wairz-intake-sweep-2026-04-19 session 7e8dd7c3: mobsfscan_service.py was deleted in Phase 5 part 4 split (commit 206fbd5); module no longer exists. Use from app.services.mobsfscan import ... instead (MobsfScanPipeline, MobsfScanFinding, get_mobsfscan_pipeline, mobsfscan_available, normalize_mobsfscan_findings, SUPPRESSED_PATH_PATTERNS, SUPPRESSED_RULES all re-exported).

custom.name: auto-frontend-multipart-no-explicit-timeout
custom.message: Multipart upload endpoints must declare a timeout. File uploads up to MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB (default 2 GB) can take several minutes on slow links; the default axios 30s fires mid-upload surfacing a fake 'upload failed'. Use UPLOAD_TIMEOUT=600_000 (10 min) per the firmware.ts / documents.ts / kernels.ts pattern. Learned from session 7e8dd7c3 long-op timeout sweep.

custom.name: auto-q4-no-get-analysis-cache
custom.message: Learned from session 480666ce (Q4): GhidraAnalysisCache class + get_analysis_cache() singleton removed in commit a7bfe47. Use module-level ghidra_service.X() directly — e.g. await ghidra_service.get_functions(...). For tests, patch the module binding: patch('module.ghidra_service', mock_cache) with positional 2nd arg, not return_value=.

custom.name: auto-module-level-asyncio-lock
custom.message: Module-level asyncio.Lock() construction runs at import time, before any event loop. On workers / mcp_server / strict-async contexts this can raise 'no running event loop'. Safe pattern: declare `_lock: asyncio.Lock | None = None` + helper `def _get_lock(): global _lock; if _lock is None: _lock = asyncio.Lock(); return _lock`. Learned from session 480666ce Q4 Ghidra singleton drop — see ghidra_service.py:202-216.

custom.name: auto-ci-pytest-ignore-requires-intake
custom.message: CI pytest --ignore= flags hide real signal. Each ignored file MUST have a tracking intake in .planning/intake/*-unstable-*.md with per-file failure triage (test-bug / product-bug / missing-fixture / deprecated). Remove the --ignore= line in the same commit that makes the file green. Learned from session 480666ce backend-tests.yml workflow — see .planning/intake/backend-pytest-unstable-tests.md.

custom.name: auto-vendor-aes-followups-1
custom.message: Learned from campaign vendor-aes-followups-2026-04-21: _run_hardware_firmware_detection_safe must NOT be spawned from inside unpack_firmware. Fire it AFTER the caller commits (arq_worker.unpack_firmware_job or routers/firmware._run_unpack_background), or the concurrent DB write will clobber vendor_decryption + detection_roots. See commit bede8a5.

custom.name: auto-pytest-no-hasattr-against-mock
custom.message: MagicMock/AsyncMock auto-creates any attribute on access, so `hasattr(mock, 'X_invoked')` always returns True. Use `mock.X.assert_not_called()` / `mock.X.assert_called_once()` instead. Seen in test_cache_module.py:215 pre-fix (session 2026-04-23, commit 81949b7).

custom.name: auto-pytest-uuid-str-in-compiled-sql
custom.message: SQLAlchemy renders UUIDs in compiled SQL as hex literals WITHOUT dashes. `str(uuid)` produces the dashed form and will never be a substring of the compiled SQL. Use `<uuid>.hex in compiled` or `str(<uuid>).replace('-', '') in compiled`. Seen in test_cache_module.py:233 pre-fix (session 2026-04-23, commit 81949b7).

custom.name: auto-pytest-mock-patch-androguard-at-service
custom.message: Androguard primitives (APK, AnalyzeAPK, DEX, dx) are typically lazy-imported inside service function bodies from androguard.core.apk / androguard.misc — so patching them at the service module is a no-op. Patch the SOURCE module instead (e.g. `patch('androguard.core.apk.APK')`). Triple-discovered across 3 streams in session 2026-04-23 (commits 7941f0f / 1da1f28 / 5e5eda0).

custom.name: auto-cpe-dictionary-direct-instantiation
custom.message: Direct instantiation of CpeDictionaryService bypasses the module's singleton accessor (cpe_dictionary_service.py:354 -> get_cpe_dictionary_service). Per-call instantiation OOMs under multi-blob scans because each instance loads the 37268-product CPE index into a per-instance dict (see /tmp/wairz-smoke-logs.txt 2026-04-24 OOM, 11x CPE loads from cve_matcher._match_chipset_cpe). The ONLY legitimate site is cpe_dictionary_service.py:354 itself (the singleton accessor body). All other sites must use get_cpe_dictionary_service(). See .planning/knowledge/gui-smoke-bugs-2026-04-24-antipatterns.md.

custom.name: auto-firmware-upload-409-frontend-error-unwrap
custom.message: Learned from campaign firmware-upload-duplicate-409-2026-04-26: bare `err instanceof Error ? err.message` clobbers FastAPI's response.data.detail with axios's framework default 'Request failed with status code N'. Use extractErrorMessage(err, '<context-specific fallback>') from @/utils/error instead. See .planning/intake/frontend-error-message-unwrap-sweep.md.

custom.name: auto-frontend-error-inline-detail-extract
custom.message: Learned from autopilot frontend-error-message-unwrap-sweep-2026-04-29: avoid hand-rolled `(err as { response?: ... }).response?.data?.detail` inline detail extraction at display sites. Use extractErrorMessage(err, '<context-specific fallback>') from @/utils/error — the helper does the same FastAPI-detail-aware unwrap and avoids per-site drift. Companion to auto-firmware-upload-409-frontend-error-unwrap (which catches the bare `instanceof Error ? e.message` form). See .planning/knowledge/frontend-error-message-unwrap-sweep-2026-04-29-patterns.md.

custom.name: auto-audit-2026-05-04-mock-call-count-without-args
custom.message: Learned from audit-2026-05-04: tests asserting `mock_db.add.call_count == N` without also capturing `call_args_list` cannot catch value-flow bugs (Rule #35b — the confidence-NULL bug shipped because tests only counted calls). Pair every `add.call_count == N` with a `call_args_list` capture that asserts the constructor args of each persisted entity. See .planning/knowledge/audit-2026-05-04-antipatterns.md anti-pattern #2.

custom.name: auto-audit-2026-05-04-finding-direct-construct
custom.message: Learned from audit-2026-05-04: direct `Finding(...)` construction outside FindingService.create() bypasses field-forwarding logic (audit found 5 such sites — confidence + firmware_id silently dropped). Route through FindingService.create() instead. The ONLY legitimate site is finding_service.py itself. See .planning/knowledge/audit-2026-05-04-antipatterns.md anti-pattern #4.

custom.name: auto-audit-intakes-2026-05-05-ci-silent-zero
custom.message: Learned from audit-intakes-wave1-wave2-2026-05-05 (Rule #35a generalisation): the `2>/dev/null || echo 0` pattern in CI parse steps deliberately discards subprocess errors and reports a falsy zero — a broken scan / parse / count appears 'clean' indistinguishably from a real green run. Replace with: `set -euo pipefail` at the top of the run-block, capture via `out=$(cmd)` (NOT process substitution which decouples the inner exit code), let non-zero exits abort the step. If a count genuinely defaults to 0 in some condition, branch in python with explicit try/except + sys.exit(non-zero) on parse failure. See .planning/knowledge/audit-intakes-wave1-wave2-2026-05-05-antipatterns.md anti-pattern #1.

custom.name: auto-phase-2-test-coverage-2026-05-06-lazy-import-patch-target
custom.message: Learned from phase-2-test-coverage-routers-services-2026-05-06 (extends Rule #30 androguard rule to the broader lazy-imported library family). These libraries (weasyprint / setools / pypdf / clamd / rapidfuzz / jadx / lief / pefile / cpu_rec / qiling) are typically lazy-imported inside service function bodies — patching them at the service module is a silent no-op. Use SOURCE-patch: `patch.dict(sys.modules, {"<libname>": fake_module})` for full-module replacement, paired with a `not hasattr(consumer_module, "<libname>")` sentinel that fails LOUDLY if a future refactor promotes the import to top-level. See .planning/knowledge/phase-2-test-coverage-routers-services-patterns.md pattern #2 + .planning/knowledge/phase-2-test-coverage-routers-services-antipatterns.md anti-pattern #3.

custom.name: auto-phase-2-test-coverage-2026-05-06-stale-nested-tests-docker-cp
custom.message: Learned from phase-2-test-coverage-routers-services-2026-05-06 anti-pattern #5: relative-path `docker cp tests/test_X.py <container>:/app/tests/test_X.py` invocations from inside `backend/` land files at `/app/tests/tests/test_X.py` (nested) instead of `/app/tests/test_X.py` due to host-CWD-prefix interpretation. The stale dir accumulates outdated test files across sessions and produces phantom failures in full-suite smoke runs. Use HOST-ABSOLUTE paths in `docker cp`: `docker cp /home/<user>/code/wairz/backend/tests/test_X.py <container>:/app/tests/test_X.py`. See .planning/knowledge/phase-2-test-coverage-routers-services-antipatterns.md anti-pattern #5.

custom.name: auto-final-eps2c-zeta1-2026-05-09-mcp-count-eq-assertion
custom.message: Learned from windows-coverage-godmode final (Rule-of-Three): use `>=` for growing-collection counts (MCP registry, finding-source allowlist). Equality assertions break at every phase boundary that adds tools/sources. Move the phase-shipping count to a docstring; relax the assertion.

custom.name: auto-final-eps2c-zeta1-2026-05-09-finding-source-eq-count
custom.message: Learned from windows-coverage-godmode final: use `>=` for the WindowsFindingSource Literal value count. Equality breaks every time the cross-stack alignment slice extends ck_findings_source.

custom.name: auto-final-eps2c-zeta1-2026-05-09-pr-close-comment-flag
custom.message: Learned from windows-coverage-godmode final: `gh pr close --comment` is unsupported in some gh versions. Use two-step: `gh pr comment <N> --body "..."` then `gh pr close <N>`.

custom.name: auto-async-cleanup-2026-05-11-no-bare-async-noqa
custom.message: Learned from async-cleanup-2026-05-11 Rule #43: bare `# noqa: ASYNC<code>` without a rationale is prohibited. Add `— <rationale>` matching one of the 4 categories: (1) pre-flight stat before bounded sync subprocess; (2) pure-string path math (no filesystem I/O); (3) bounded loop over ≤3 detection roots (Rule #16 partner); (4) caller-supplied timeout per Rule #29 contract. Future code review can REJECT a noqa whose rationale doesn't fit a category.

custom.name: auto-async-cleanup-2026-05-11-no-f823-noqa
custom.message: Learned from async-cleanup-2026-05-11 Rule #40: F823 (local variable used before assignment) is mechanical — Python's local-binding rule promotes function-body imports to function-scope locals so any pre-import reference raises UnboundLocalError. Fix AT SOURCE by moving the `import X` to the first statement of the function body. NEVER noqa F823. Worked example: `app/ai/tools/emulation.py:2627` — `import asyncio` moved from mid-function to first statement (commit `6376d8d` Phase D.39).

custom.name: auto-async-cleanup-2026-05-11-pipe-then-exit-capture
custom.message: Learned from async-cleanup-2026-05-11 Rule #35a/Antipattern A1 (reinforcement): `cmd | tail|head|grep|jq|awk|sed; echo $?` captures the PIPE's last-command exit, NOT the original cmd's. To capture the real exit: `cmd; ec=$?` BEFORE the pipe, or use `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` after the pipeline, or `set -o pipefail` before the pipe. The Bash tool does NOT enable pipefail by default. Companion to existing rule `auto-audit-intakes-2026-05-05-ci-silent-zero` which covers the `2>/dev/null || echo 0` variant.

custom.name: auto-windows-coverage-godmode-eta-2026-05-11-regex-word-boundary-non-word-prefix
custom.message: Learned from windows-coverage-godmode-eta-2026-05-11 (Rule-of-Two: η.B classifier `\\b-enc\\b` + η.C classifier `\\b\\[char\\[\\]\\]\\(` independently failed): regex `\\b` word-boundary metachar does NOT match between two non-word characters or at string-start when next char is non-word. So `\\b-enc\\b` silently fails to match the literal `-enc` flag at string-start. Symptom: classifier returns None on intended targets; tier-1 test catches if present. Fix: use explicit `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9])<token>(?:[^A-Za-z0-9]|$)` lookarounds for adjacency-to-non-word checks. Mechanical detection: any classifier regex containing `\\b` followed by a non-word character is suspect.

custom.name: auto-windows-coverage-godmode-eta-2026-05-12-in-container-system-python
custom.message: Learned from windows-coverage-godmode-eta-2026-05-12 antipattern #10: `docker compose exec backend python -c '...'` resolves `python` to the BASE IMAGE's system Python (no wairz deps installed) — emits `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sqlalchemy'` on the first import even though `/app/.venv` has the dep. Use `/app/.venv/bin/python` explicitly. Already codified in CLAUDE.md Rule #20 caveat (`docker compose exec -T -w /app -e PYTHONPATH=/app backend /app/.venv/bin/<tool>`) — this rule enforces the discipline mechanically across docs / scripts / agent prompts.

custom.name: auto-local-dev-env-no-auth-2026-05-12-rebuild-without-restartcount-probe
custom.message: Learned from local-dev-env-no-auth-2026-05-12 (`wairz-backend-1` restart-looped 118 cycles across 5+ sessions because rebuild success was declared without probing `RestartCount`): after ANY `docker compose up -d --build backend|worker|migrator`, also probe `docker inspect wairz-backend-1 --format '{{.RestartCount}}'` AND `docker compose ps backend` AND `docker compose logs --tail 20 backend` BEFORE trusting the rebuild. The backend container's lifespan check at `app/main.py:68-76` exits **78 (EX_CONFIG)** if neither `API_KEY` nor `WAIRZ_ALLOW_NO_AUTH=true` is in `.env` — and the worker stays healthy regardless, so worker-uptime is NOT evidence backend is up. See `.mex/patterns/post-rebuild-health-check.md` for the full discipline and CLAUDE.md Rule #8 for the rebuild scope.

custom.name: auto-rule-44-deep-review-2026-05-14-alembic-timestamp-nullable
custom.message: Learned from Rule #44 backfill deep-review 2026-05-14: alembic migrations that create *_at columns with server_default=sa.func.now() MUST also declare nullable=False if the ORM column is Mapped[datetime] (non-Optional). Otherwise alembic-autogenerate-empty detects modify_nullable drift on CI. See postmortem section 'What Broke #1' + recommendation #2.

custom.name: auto-bt-yaml-externalization-2026-05-17-non-qualcomm-cna-braktooth-cves
custom.message: Learned from campaign bt-yaml-externalization-session-2026-05-17: CVE-2021-28139 (ESP32 RCE) / -34147 (Cypress WICED) / -31609 (Silicon Labs iWRAP) / -31612 (Zhuhai Jieli AC69xx) are NOT Qualcomm-CNA per NVD CPE. The only Qualcomm-CNA BrakTooth-DoS CVE per NVD is CVE-2021-30348. Pinning any of these 4 under a qca_rome family pin replicates the recursive disclosure-batch antipattern (Reviewer B 2026-05-16 + 2026-05-17 catches). Verify per-CVE NVD CPE before adding.

custom.name: auto-bt-yaml-externalization-2026-05-17-nonexistent-mcp-tool-names

Actual hardware-firmware tools: analyze_hardware_firmware, check_firmware_cves, run_vulnerability_scan (backend/app/ai/tools/{hardware_firmware,sbom}.py). custom.name: auto-hw-firmware-adaptive-2026-05-18-device-metadata-overwrite
custom.message: Learned from campaign hw-firmware-adaptive-session-2026-05-18: assigning a fresh dict to firmware.device_metadata OVERWRITES prior keys (e.g. detection_roots written by upstream callers). Mirror the merge-then-stamp pattern at firmware_paths.py:787-791 — load existing via _normalize_firmware_device_metadata, dict-copy, set the new key, stamp. Reviewer A B1-HIGH 2026-05-18.

custom.name: auto-hw-firmware-adaptive-2026-05-18-realtek-offset-8-project-id
custom.message: Learned from campaign hw-firmware-adaptive-session-2026-05-18: Realtek BT firmware project_id is NOT at offset 8 per upstream drivers/bluetooth/btrtl.h. Offset 8..11 is __le32 fw_version (v1) or __u8 fw_version[8] (v2). project_id is encoded as TLV records at the FILE TAIL — reverse-scan for (opcode=0, length=1, data=PID). Use _scan_realtek_project_id_from_tail in parsers/bt_firmware_banner.py. Scout C 2026-05-18 catch.

The generic MtimeCachedYamlLoader[T] now lives at backend/app/utils/yaml_cache.py — use `from app.utils.yaml_cache import MtimeCachedYamlLoader` instead. Old hw-firmware path is gone.

custom.name: auto-hw-firmware-adaptive-2026-05-18-low-confidence-curated-tier
custom.message: Learned from campaign hw-firmware-adaptive-session-2026-05-18: _match_curated MUST skip blobs with detection_confidence='low' (F-FORENSIC-11 Reviewer B 2026-05-18). The Realtek BT parser's soft-fallback path emits vendor=realtek/confidence=low for any [Rr]ealte[ck] ASCII match — these blobs MUST NOT receive curated-tier CVE attribution. Test: test_match_curated_skips_low_confidence_blob.

custom.name: auto-bare-metal-rule52-1-jsonb-cast-in-orm
custom.message: Learned from campaign bare-metal-mcu-rule52-phase1-phase2 (hotfix 8c1b740): ORM `server_default=text("'{}'::jsonb")` is Postgres-only — the `::jsonb` cast renders verbatim under SQLite and breaks 749 `_live_db` tests with `unrecognized token: ':'`. Use `server_default=text("'{}'")` instead — the column type already carries JSONB constraint. Alembic migrations MAY use `::jsonb` (Postgres-only); ORM must be dialect-agnostic. Mirrors `HardwareFirmwareBlob.metadata_:60` convention.

custom.name: auto-bare-metal-rule52-2-yaml-dsl-keys
custom.message: Learned from campaign bare-metal-mcu-rule52-phase1-phase2 (CLAUDE.md Rule #52 hard cap): chip-family YAML is DATA, never code. NO `regex` / `script` / `template` / `predicate` / `lua` / `expression` / `eval_python` keys EVER. Pydantic `extra='forbid'` rejects these at load time; this rule catches them at commit time. Extending the closed grammar requires Rule #25 single-slice cross-stack alignment (DB CHECK + Pydantic Literal + frontend Config mirror) + Rule #46 META-CANARY — not a YAML edit.

custom.name: auto-bare-metal-rule52-3-frontend-inline-comment-in-config-map
custom.message: Learned from campaign bare-metal-mcu-rule52-phase1-phase2 (P1.9 alignment-test failure): `//` comments interleaved between entries in `FINDING_SOURCE_CONFIG` (or similar parsed object literals) break the alignment-test parser at `tests/test_finding_source_alignment.py::_parse_finding_source_config_keys`. The parser's regex `^\s*['\"]?([\w\-]+)['\"]?\s*:` doesn't match `//`. Operator-facing context belongs in the schema docstring or a sibling design doc, NOT interleaved comments. Section-header comments (above the whole block) are fine; per-entry comments are not.

custom.name: auto-file-format-rule52-1
custom.message: Learned from campaign file-format-yaml-registry-2026-05-19: file_formats YAML must NOT declare open-predicate keys (regex/script/template/eval/lua/vql/predicate/expression) — closed-grammar schema-driven discipline per CLAUDE.md Rule #52. Closed Literals only where YAML maps to executable Python.

custom.name: auto-file-format-rule52-2
custom.message: Learned from campaign file-format-yaml-registry-2026-05-19: manifest_source: _system is RESERVED for data/file_formats/_system/ tier (wairz invariants, precedence [0,9]). Operator-supplied YAMLs cannot outrank wairz invariants — schema model_validator rejects this at catalog load.

custom.name: auto-file-format-rule52-3
custom.message: Learned from campaign file-format-yaml-registry-2026-05-19: detection.always_matches: true is reserved for the SINGLE _system/linux_blob_fallback.yaml sentinel (sentinel-cardinality META-CANARY enforces). Operator manifests must declare specific detection signals.

custom.name: auto-file-format-rule52-4
custom.message: Learned from campaign file-format-yaml-registry-2026-05-19: evaluation_mode: first_match is FORBIDDEN — first-match was the bug shape (Scout GG §SC5 generalized). Only Literal value today is 'best_match'; resolver collects ALL matches then sorts by total-order tuple.

custom.name: auto-file-format-p32-1-plugins-no-subprocess
custom.message: Learned from campaign file-format-yaml-registry-p32-2026-05-19: bundled file-format plugins MUST NOT import subprocess / requests / httpx / aiohttp / socket / urllib (Rule #36 + Rule #45 + M8 META-CANARY discipline). The worker is the security boundary; plugins must be parse-only against the in-process blob_head. Operator out-of-tree plugins via WAIRZ_FORMAT_PLUGIN_PATH defer to P4 side-container (Exception 3) where the isolation is at the container level, not the plugin level.

custom.name: auto-file-format-p32-2-system-dispatch-default-rank-check
custom.message: Learned from campaign file-format-yaml-registry-p32-2026-05-19: _system/*.yaml manifest declaring dispatch.default pointing to a core-tier format_id triggers A6 dispatch-rank-monotonicity WARN (attestation split _system → core). For unknown-family fallback, set the manifest's own output.classifier_format to the desired fallback value and drop dispatch.default. Reference: _system/rtos_dispatch.yaml comment explaining the design choice.

custom.name: auto-file-format-p32-3-text-format-evaluator-no-hardcoded-bytes
custom.message: Learned from campaign file-format-yaml-registry-p32-2026-05-19: hardcoded byte literals like b':', b'S', b'@', b'#' in resolver.py violate Rule #52 closed-grammar discipline + M5 anti-hardcode META-CANARY. Every byte the text-format evaluator compares against MUST come from signal.text_format_constraint (record_start_byte_hex / charset / terminator_record_hex). Allowlist b'' + b'\n' + b'\r' + b'\r\n' (mechanical terminator-stripping constants — declared in _TEXT_FORMAT_TERMINATORS table).

custom.name: auto-substring-in-head-2026-05-20-in-container-pytest-tests
custom.message: Learned from campaign substring-in-head-signal-2026-05-20 (antipattern #2): `docker compose exec backend (uv run )?(pytest|python) tests/...` fails because backend/.dockerignore (commit b9f438f, 2026-04-18) excludes `tests/` from the production image. Use HOST execution instead: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests/...` or `cd backend && uv run python tests/fixtures/.../_GENERATE.py`. The host's `backend/.venv` has the same `uv.lock`-resolved deps as the container. NEVER use `docker compose exec` for paths under tests/, alembic/versions/, .ruff_cache/, .planning/, docs/, *.md, .citadel/, or .claude/ — all are .dockerignore'd.

custom.name: auto-sbom-regr-session1-2026-05-21-bare-create-task-background
custom.message: Learned from campaign sbom-vuln-scan-regression-session1-2026-05-21 (antipattern #6): bare `asyncio.create_task(_run_*_background(...))` in routers has GC-vanish risk — the asyncio scheduler only keeps a WEAK reference, so the task can be collected mid-run on memory pressure, leaving the firmware row stuck in `*_status='running'` forever and the frontend in a stuck-polling loop (Scout D primary symptom for the 2026-05-21 regression). Use `_spawn_background_task(coro, name=...)` from a shared helper (currently lives in `routers/sbom.py`; will be factored into `app/utils/background.py` per Session 2 sweep) that keeps a strong reference in a module-level set + auto-discards on completion via `add_done_callback`. Documented at https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task — 'Important: Save a reference to the result of this function, to avoid a task disappearing mid-execution.'

custom.name: auto-sbom-regr-session1-2026-05-21-too-narrow-mock-create-task
custom.message: Learned from campaign sbom-vuln-scan-regression-session1-2026-05-21 (antipattern #3): a too-narrow mock signature `def fake_create_task(coro):` breaks when production widens to pass `name=...` — TypeError: got an unexpected keyword argument 'name'. Use `def fake_create_task(coro, *, name=None)` or `def fake_create_task(coro, **kwargs)` so mock shims are forward-compatible with future signature widening. Rule #30 sibling discipline — when widening a public function signature, every mock that patches the function needs review.
